attempts.raw_response: Make sure to bend your knees slightly upon landing to absorb the impact and protect your joints. Practice on a soft surface like a gymnastics mat before attempting this on a hard floor. Start by practicing the hurdle approach separately from the cartwheel motion. Once comfortable, work on combining the two movements slowly at first. Keep your core tight throughout the entire rotation to maintain control. Many beginners make the mistake of separating their hands or feet, so practice the simultaneous hand placement and foot plant. Have a spotter nearby when learning this skill. Build up your shoulder and core strength with conditioning exercises. Once mastered, the round off becomes a fundamental skill for more advanced tumbling passes.

pair.human_continuation:
To do a back handspring immediately afterwards, you need to use the momentum of the roundoff to help you generate even more speed. Here's what you do:  Get in a seated position with your arms swinging up over your head. Push through your toes to lift your arms up even more. Fall backwards, taking care not to arch your back too much. Plant your hands on the floor, with your fingers facing away from you. Swing your legs over your hands, so you're in a hand stand for a second. Keep your feet together as you plant them on the floor. Pop up with your hands above your head.
It's important to stretch out your body, especially your back, before you do a full twisting layout.
